text_fidelity_a:
Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+ If you, like me, are looking for games to play with a high energy, lack of focus little boy, then this is the game for you. For my four year old, games with a lot of rules and that require skills he's still learning with clear winners and losers are not the best choice games for us. He doesn't have the patience, skill, or temperament. I needed games to slowly introduce him into those skills and Pop Up Pirate is that game! The only rule, everyone takes turns to place a sword into a slot. The person who makes the pirate pop-up out of the barrel wins. We don't play winner/loser, but you can if you choose to do so.

The game comes with 20 swords, four colors with five each, a barrel, and said pirate. It's for 2 to 4 players, my son and I just pick up a sword no matter the color, but if you have more kids or players, then you can choose colors. You stick the pirate in the barrel where there is a trap/spring mechanism that is only triggered when someone sticks a sword in the right slot. Each player takes a color and everyone takes turns sticking a sword into a slot. When the right sword pokes the pirate, he pops high up into the air. The pirate is fairly light weight so if he were to really go flying he would not break anything or hurt anyone. The pirate jumps at most 2 feet into the air, probably less. The only caveat is to make kids aren't sticking their face near the barrel with the pirate in the hole for obvious reasons. This game comes in fairly big box as the barrel is about as wide as a clothes iron, but not nearly as tall.

If you need a game for toddlers/preschoolers that is guaranteed to teach taking turns and highly giggle inducing, then Pop up Pirate is your game!
text_fidelity_b: Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+

Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.
text_fidelity_b: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys…

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad

text_fidelity_a:
Magic the Gathering Cards - Khans of Tarkir - Booster Packs (6 Pack Lot) I ordered 18 boosters (3 of 6 booster bundles) and two of the bundles showed signs of being tampered with. Extra cuts on the bottom edge of the pack, packs that were ridiculously easy to open -- I've never opened boosters that basically fall apart along one crimped edge consistently like these did. I really don't trust that someone hasn't sorted through these and skimmed the fetch lands out or something. I can't prove that they were tampered with, the right numbers of cards were all there in the right proportions, but it sure feel like this is some kind of scam the way those packs fell apart.

tl;dr: Stay away, get your boosters from sealed product like sealed booster boxes, sealed fat packs or sealed holiday boxes instead; the packs I got in bagged bundles from my seller were fishy as hell.
text_fidelity_b: Magic the Gathering Cards - Khans of Tarkir - Booster Packs (6 Pack Lot)

text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! text_fidelity_a:
Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+) Luvabella is quite an incredible doll, as the more your child plays with her, the more she learns and does. At first glance, she's quite plain, hard- not cuddly soft and has huge eyes with real eyelashes. The minute you put her 4 "C" batteries in (Doll does not come with batteries, you have to buy them), she comes to life with the cutest expressions, movements and baby babble speech. And incredibly, she speaks either English or French. (Coming from Canada, it's only natural- but of course she's made in China.)

Luvabella has a cute dress and hairbow, bottle, spoon, pacifier and lamb toy. When you give her the baby bottle, she easily goes to sleep, especially if you sing to her. When you feed her with the spoon, she chews and if you didn't feed her enough, she'll let you know. When she cries and gets fussy, waving her arms, her pacifier soothes her. Her lamb toy makes her make babble and animal sounds and the more she plays with the lamb, the more she learns more animal sounds and more animal names.

As the child plays with Luvabella, she does more and more. Touch her chest and hear her heart beat. Touch her feet, and she talks and calls you Mama. The baby babble will grow into words and eventually phrases. She even kisses her little Lamby toy and makes cute animal sounds. When you tickle her, she giggles and waves her arms. She plays peek-a-boo and laughs while you play with her, and eventually you'll hear her say "I see you". To have a conversation, hold her feet while speaking, she will answer back first in babble, then in words, then in phrases. As you speak and play with her, you never know what she'll do- either smile, cry, giggle or laugh. She constantly changes her responses and learns more vocabulary, and if your child gets tired of English, you can also hear her in French. This is a doll that gets cuter as she comes to life and keeps learning more, and your child will find her a wonderful challenge that never gets boring! A big 5 Stars for 2017.
text_fidelity_b: Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+)

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. text_fidelity_a:
UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.

text_fidelity_a: WE Games 4 Player Shut The Box Dice Board Game with Lid- Walnut Stained Wood - Large Coffee Table Size - 14 Inches, for Family and Adult Game Night Play in Classroom, Home or Bar Product listing says 12 yrs and up. Don't listen to it. If you have kids as young as 4 and starting to learn adding and subtracting, this game will be super educational! My youngest is 5 and she bugs us every day to play this game. Kids under 12 will love this game, trust me. It's not just adding and subtracting, for more advance play, you can do multiplication, division, any math you can think of. Lets say your roll a 4 and a 3, but you're out of tiles to make 7. But you have a 9 and a 3 in play, well if multiplication is part of the game then 4x3 is 12, hence, you can shut the 9 and 3 tiles. Lets say you roll a 5 and a 4, but you have no more tiles that add up to 9, but you have a 3 in play. What's the square root of 9? It's 3, now you can shut that 3. Any math you can think of is fair game, that's how we play it. Play this game with your kids, and they will learn math faster! 5-Stars.

There are plenty of toys to choose from, and there are even a few that cater to the preferences of kids preschool age and younger. My Little Pony So Soft Pinkie Pie is certainly one of them. It takes the My Little Pony character and redesigns it to a toddler's preferences by making it cuter and more cuddly.

My Little Pony So Soft Pinkie Pie is battery operated and the reason for the batteries is that this toy can talk. Lift Pinkie Pie by the hand and pretend to help her walk and she will respond with: Look, I can walk! Pretend to feed her and she will say: More please. She says other phrases, too, like I Love You Mommy and Excuse Me. The phrases are stated at random and each one is activated by lifting the hand. However, make sure you don't leave the toy Try mode because if you do, it will talk whenever someone passes by. Turn the control to the On position and it will only talk when the hand is moved.

My Little Pony Pinkie Pie is made from plastic and that makes the toy basically unbreakable. It can be dropped, thrown, etc., without worry. The toy comes complete with the My Little Pony Pinkie Pie doll, a bottle, pacifier, bowl, and spoon. The added accessories are great for the young mommies in your house who will enjoy playing with, feeding, and taking care of their little friend. The doll is light so children of most any age can easily lift it and carry it around. And the doll is very cute and babyish in appearance, which will add to its appeal to the young ones in the home.

My Little Pony So Soft Pinkie Pie is a hit with both of my young girls and they rate it as an enjoyable toy. They may not rank it in their top five, but they still like this toy and have not grown tired of it since it was introduced in our home several weeks ago.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game When I first asked my family if I should get this game, they were not quite sure what to think. We went and looked at a bunch of videos and it looked really good. So, I ordered it. Then I watched a few more videos and wondered.. did I make a mistake?

WHAT IS THIS GAME LIKE?
This game is based upon a book. I have not read the book so if you are concerned that might affect your like of this game, keep in mind that I had no idea about this series of books, so it did not affect game play for me.

The game comes with a board that folds into a fourth of its size- a real plus for storage. It has a plastic storage area which holds all of the pieces- and yes, there are pieces. You press out the cardboard pieces so that you can keep them to play the game in the future. It is not hard to do and they pressed out cleanly.

There are cards and several sets of dice. Each player gets a set of dice. Maximum players are four. You can play successfully with two players.

HOW IS THE GAME TO LEARN?
I have to admit when we got the game, I was overtired, and very frustrated as it was. When one of our kids wanted to play, I was so afraid that I made a mistake and would hate this game. It really overwhelmed me. I could not make heads or tails of the instructions, and when trying to watch videos, well ,I was SURE I made a mistake in choosing this game.

Finally our child said, "How about we just try to play and walk through it?" I was not in the mood, but knew I had to test this out.

So... out came the very detailed instruction booklet. The beginning to set it up did not take too long, but it was not starting to make sense yet. I was not thrilled. Then as we read each move and worked through it, I was having a headache.

I kept with it, and about a half hour into the game, suddenly it all began to make sense. Then suddenly, I was enjoying it. In fact, I could not wait to play it again!

WHO MIGHT LIKE THIS GAME?
My kids who liked this were early teens and above range. It is really beautifully rendered, the cards and pieces are interesting, and the board itself is really nice to look at. It needs to be played at a nice table with room on it- like you might use for Monopoly or Life.

I would say that anyone who enjoys history, games that have purpose, and home educators might enjoy playing this game. It is not boring, nor is it a thrill ride, but it is a nice entertaining game that is interesting and did keep my attention.

If someone has an overabundance of energy and can not sit still unless entertained by a screen in constant motion, this might not work out for them. If someone has patience and enjoys artworks and interesting things (like playing with Legos or other similar things) this might be a game to try out for them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite being a bit overwhelmed at first, once we plunged into the game, after a little while, I found it fun, interesting to play and found myself looking forward to playing it over again which is the same sentiment from the rest of the family as they have played it too.

MY RATING
Five stars for this. If you watch videos, don't get too overwhelmed, just plunge in and play it as a learning experience and it will suddenly click and off you go. I have to say it is one of the limited number of board games that make me want to play again and I look forward to it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game

text_fidelity_a: Warashibe Wooden Secret Puzzle Box, 5 Sun 21 Steps, Japan Made, with Original Gift Box I have some from the 1940s that my father brought home from World War II.  One is more traditional - it is made of wood and looks like a stack of faux books with a larger book on its side both on the bottom and top.  The "page" piece of the bottom book slides open to an area that holds the key, the bottom book slides back, the center book's spine slides down to reveal the keyhole.  Insert the key, turn it and the book on top opens to a velvet lined interior.  The top book has several veneers to create a border and little birds flying across the top.  My other puzzle box has a large veneered diamond on top of the heavily veneered box.  Slide the diamond back and the box can be opened.  Center the diamond on the closed box and it "locks" it.  This box is more complicated that either of my other puzzle boxes mentioned here, but one thing they all share in common is the veneer work.  This box features very geometric veneering and it is quite pretty.  The complexity of the puzzle to open the box is a lot more fun and interesting for this box - it's really neat!  Yes, they are expensive, but for a reason - the veneer work and all the moving parts of this box requires a seriously high amount of quality control.  Worth it, for sure!

* Nothing I can think of. The price is just right for what you're getting. I don't recall an actual arcade game in the past called Akedo. It seems this toy is simply inspired by all the classic arcade fighting games such as Street Fighter, Fatal Fury, Tekken, etc. It will keep your children occupied for awhile and away from tablets.

One more thing, the two default figures that's already installed in the arena have clear bands wrapped around them. We saw the vertical bands on their bodies and cut them off. So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. 5-Stars!

text_fidelity_a:
Nature Bound Bug Catcher Critter Barn Habitat for Indoor/Outdoor Insect Collecting with Light Kit, White Very cool when used with adult supervision and a LOT of info about what is humane and what isn't. I've definitely seen some kids use this type of cage as a permanent home for their reptiles or frogs, and that is 100% wrong. Animals need space, and while keeping a terrarium can be great for kids to learn about living things, life, death, responsibility, etc, parents are obligated to do research on what size is correct for what animal(s) to ensure they have a decent quality of life.

Having said all that, this is not meant to be a permanent home for any sort of reptile or amphibian. It's a place to observe creatures for a Short time, and then release them. For that use, it is fine. For anything longer than a couple of days, it is cruel.

Some neat features: the light (of course!), a ruler at the bottom so kids can measure the animal without handling or harassing them too much, a magnifying lens (but it only works a little--you need to be in the right spot for that to do anything), and a little mini lid on top, which is especially useful if there's a reptile, amphibian, or spider inside, and you want to introduce an insect for it to eat.

Nice hands-on educational potential!
text_fidelity_b: Nature Bound Bug Catcher Critter Barn Habitat for Indoor/Outdoor Insect Collecting with Light Kit, White

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition A nice update to an old game. I threw this in my shopping cart while out Christmas shopping. So I did not buy it on Amazon, but I am an Amazon Prime member. Cars 3 Monopoly Jr. is played just like regular Monopoly Jr. Only the pieces, property names, and chance cards have a Cars 3 theme. The rules are exactly the same. For those of you who do not know, Monopoly Jr. is a simplified version of Monopoly. You don't build houses or hotels. Mortgages on property is not a thing. The money is also way more simple. You still go to "jail." You will collect $2. However, there is literally no strategy involved. Just be the one to have the most money once one person goes bankrupt and you win. Monopoly Jr. does not end in arguments or tears (so long as your child can handle the issue of losing, which I will explain later.) Monopoly Jr. will not be the source of a deep rift through the family. You will find that you're still friends with people after the game is over. Game play is fast, you will not be playing into the wee hours of the morning trying to negotiate a loan because you landed on Park Place.

I like board games because it gets me and my son together and playing together. Screens are not involved. However, do understand that teaching 3-5 year olds how to play board games is a long process. At the end of the day, the point of playing games like this with kids this young is to get them using various skills. Skills such as paying attention, following multiple steps, counting, and taking turns. I would recommend holding off on competitive board games until after you have played a few cooperative board games. Such as [[ASIN:B006S9MUPU Peaceable Kingdom / Race to the Treasure! Cooperative Board Game]] or [[ASIN:B002V3RCE6 Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It]] Why? Because I found it helpful to play cooperative style games after playing competitive games ended in broken pieces and a broken spirit. Now at 5, it's still tough, but he's more capable of receiving the lesson that there are winners and there are losers. If your child gets really heartbroken when they lose, definitely get cooperative games before you get this one.

I would recommend this only for children starting at 5 years of age if you have spent time playing other board games, especially cooperative style board games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay This is a really fun "spooky" game for kids. It's not really that "spooky", but it does require that you play in the dark, which can be a bit difficult for the very young, but fortunately the large hiding place pieces and the very cute shadowlings got our daughter to play the game willingly.

This is a hide-and-seek style of game in which one player moves a real, working lantern around the board trying to illuminate the shadowlings. It uses the old fashioned "roll and move" mechanic, but fortunately, the game does a good job of ensuring that you can usually get where you need to go. This is the role best suited to younger children.

Other children, or parents, will play as the Shadowlings. The lantern player closes their eyes, while the other players move shadowlings that are not illuminated in an attempt to hide them from the lantern-holding player. This role is better for adults because the rules are a little vague and open to interpretation in this area. Technically, you are allowed to move anywhere, so long as you are not illuminated and I think that's difficult for children to judge fairly (even the adults had an argument about it).

Overall, this is a good kids game, and adults can have some fun too. I wish the rules were a little clearer on how to lay out terrain, what "illuminated' really means, and so forth, but then again, too much of that would make the manual unreadable. Maybe some picture examples would have been ideal. As it is, your children will need some experience with this game with parents before you can let them play alone, but it is clever and, unlike many children's games, it's good for parents too.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay

text_fidelity_a:
CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question Excellent party game from the makers of Codenames. If you've played Codenames, then you know that is a fantastic party game, but that it requires the right group - a slow or domineering player can often mean that everyone is standing around staring at the board for an hour while they dole out perfectly configured clues. It's a fun game, but it requires the right group. That's a Question is a party game that can be played by absolutely anyone, and that, in my opinion, makes it almost a superior game.

In That's a Question!, players use cards to ask A/B style "would you rather" questions in which players attempt to guess the outcome. Based on the results, you move your pawn along the track.

The rulebook is well-written and funny, and is aware that this game is a little bit weird - attempting to give a theme to a basic Q&A style game, but it works. Of course, the game is not perfect. You are limited to only asking three different main questions, although the game does provide a wide variation of answers. There are also point modification questions which allow you to muddy up the scoring in your favor. Ultimately, the scoring was the part of the game that we found most cumbersome, and the modifiers didn't help that, simply adding a little more chaos. Scoring is also modified based on how many players are playing; as this was clearly designed as a 5-6 player game, a 4-player game has a few modifications, and the 3-player game has a fairly substantial number of scoring modifications to make it more challenging. It's nothing you can't figure out, but it is not very clean.
